guideTitle: 6 Best Under-Cabinet Motion Sensor Lights in 2026
metaDescription: Six wireless under-cabinet motion sensor lights compared by bar length, battery, color temperature options and sensor range for kitchens and closets.
introParagraphs: Under-cabinet lighting used to mean an electrician, a drilled hole and a hardwired fixture. Today a rechargeable bar with a motion sensor sticks under a shelf with a magnet or adhesive and lights the counter the moment you reach for a mug. It is one of the easiest upgrades in a kitchen, pantry or closet, and it works just as well for renters.

The differences between models come down to a short list of things. Bar length decides how much counter you can cover, battery capacity decides how often you plug in, and color temperature options decide whether the light feels cozy or crisp. A few models add a remote, and a few come in larger multipacks that suit a whole kitchen run.

We evaluated six distinct lights based on product specs and buyer feedback, weighing bar length, LED count, battery capacity, sensor range and mode options. Where a brand sells the same light in several sizes, we list it once and mention the variants.

products.name: EZVALO 5-Pack 10 inch Under Cabinet Lights with Remote
products.description:
This five light kit is built for a full run of cabinets rather than one lonely shelf. Each light has a 2400mAh rechargeable battery, a 120 degree sensor and a reach of up to 12 ft. The sensor turns the light on in 0.1 seconds, so the counter is lit before your hand arrives.

A single remote adjusts brightness, color temperature, timer settings and lighting modes for all five at once. That convenience matters when you own several lights, because walking to each one to change a setting gets old fast. The trade-off is a bigger set to charge, and the lights switch off after about 20 seconds of no motion, which is brisk if you work slowly.

Magnetic mounting keeps installation tool free. Against the 5 pack of YLXS lights at 1100mAh, the EZVALO carries more than twice the battery per bar, which means fewer removals for charging. It is the strongest pick for a kitchen with several cabinets.
products.bestFor: Kitchens with several cabinet runs where one remote should control every light.
pros: 2400mAh battery per light reduces charging trips
One remote adjusts brightness and color for all
Turns on in 0.1 seconds as you approach
Magnetic mounting needs no tools
cons: Five batteries to recharge over time
About 20 seconds of auto-off is brisk for slow tasks

products.name: MCGOR 10 inch Rechargeable Under Cabinet Lights 2 Pack
products.description:
The MCGOR pairs 40 LEDs per bar with a non-glare frosted cover, which keeps the output comfortable to look at. Five dimming levels let you choose between a soft courtesy glow and a brighter task setting. In motion mode the bar switches on automatically, and a separate always-on mode keeps it lit for longer jobs.

The always-on option is the quiet advantage, because you can leave the bar steady while chopping vegetables and then return it to motion. The drawback is that the two pack is modest, so a long counter would need to buy more or step up to the five bar kit. MCGOR also sells larger 14.7 inch bars, which we treat as the same family.

Upkeep means a periodic recharge and a wipe of the frosted cover. Compared with the Gritin at 84 LEDs per bar, the MCGOR uses fewer LEDs but keeps the design simple and glare free. It is a dependable all rounder for pantries and mid sized counters.
products.bestFor: Kitchen and pantry shelves where glare free light and easy dimming matter.
pros: Five dimming levels cover glow and task use
Frosted cover cuts glare from the 40 LEDs
Motion, always-on and off modes are simple
Magnetic design fits closets and cabinets
cons: Two bars cover only a modest counter

products.name: Gritin Under Cabinet Lighting 10.2 inch 2 Pack
products.description:
The Gritin packs 84 LEDs into a 10.2 inch bar made from aluminum alloy and durable ABS plastic. That construction feels sturdier than an all plastic strip and helps spread heat. You can pick from three color temperatures, with warm at 3000K for cozy spaces and cool at 6000K for task lighting.

Five brightness levels and four lighting modes, including OFF and Night Sensing Mode, give you the widest adjustment among the two packs. The compromise is a busier set of controls to learn, and 84 LEDs at full brightness may be more than a small shelf needs. The extra build quality also means a slightly heavier bar to hold with a magnet.

It asks for the same simple recharge routine as the others. Compared with the MCGOR at 40 LEDs and five dimming levels, the Gritin adds three color choices and a sturdier body. Pick it if you plan to leave the lights up for years.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want sturdy metal construction and wide color and mode choices.
pros: Aluminum alloy and ABS body feels sturdy
Warm 3000K to cool 6000K color choices
Five brightness levels and four modes
84 LEDs per bar give strong coverage
cons: More controls to learn than simpler bars
Slightly heavier body than plastic rivals

products.name: ZioeYiue Wireless Under Cabinet Lights 10 inch 3 Pack
products.description:
The ZioeYiue ships three 10 inch bars, which is a more useful starting count than a pair for many counters. The sensor activates within 10 ft across 120 degrees, and a power display shows how much battery remains. Three color temperatures, white, warm and natural, plus dimming, let you tune the tone.

The built-in 1800mAh battery is not detachable, and the stated runtime is 8 to 10 hours of use. The power display is the clever part, because you can see a charge coming before the light fails. The limit is that the battery cannot be swapped, so a worn cell means replacing the whole bar.

Setup is as simple as sticking or magnetizing each bar in place. Next to the EZVALO's 2400mAh per light, the ZioeYiue stores less charge but comes with a handy remaining power indicator. It is a sensible middle choice for a small kitchen.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that want three lights and a battery level readout.
pros: Three bars suit a typical small kitchen
Power display shows remaining battery
White, warm and natural color options
Dimmable with a 10 ft, 120 degree sensor
cons: Battery is built in and cannot be swapped

products.name: Rihvy 8 inch Wireless Under Cabinet Lights 3 Pack
products.description:
The Rihvy bars are the shortest at 8 inches, which makes them the easiest to tuck into tight spaces like a narrow shelf or a small cabinet. A function button switches among three color temperatures and gives stepless dimming. In AUTO mode, the motion sensor and light sensor work together so the lights only come on when it is dark and someone is near.

The included note asks you to charge them fully on arrival, which is a good habit with any rechargeable. The compromise is size, because an 8 inch bar lights less counter than the 10 inch rivals. You may need all three just to cover a short run.

The lights suit cupboards and bookshelves as well as kitchens. Compared with the ZioeYiue's 10 inch bars, the Rihvy gives up reach for discretion. It is a good pick when space under the cabinet is limited.
products.bestFor: Narrow shelves and small cabinets where a short bar fits best.
pros: 8 inch bars fit tight, narrow spaces
Stepless dimming gives precise brightness
Motion and light sensor work together in AUTO
Three color temperatures from one button
cons: Shorter bars cover less counter each
Needs a full charge before first use

products.name: YLXS 5-Pack Motion Sensor Under Cabinet Light 7.9 inch
products.description:
The YLXS gives you five compact 7.9 inch bars, each with 42 LEDs and up to 100 lumens. Three work modes include Night Mode, which lights up on motion, and three color temperatures cover warm to cool. A built-in 1100mAh battery recharges through a USB-C port.

Five lights at this size let you dot light across a closet or a pantry instead of covering only one stretch. The downside is the smallest battery of the group at 1100mAh, so each bar will need charging more often than the EZVALO's 2400mAh. A larger pack also means more lights to recharge.

Placement is easy with the compact shape, and the USB-C port means any modern cable works. Where the Rihvy offers 8 inch bars in a three pack, the YLXS adds two extra lights and a lumen figure. Pick it when you have many small spots to light.
products.bestFor: Closets and pantries with many small spots that each need a little light.
pros: Five compact bars give wide placement freedom
Up to 100 lumens from 42 LEDs per bar
USB-C charging works with common cables
Three modes and three color temperatures
cons: Short 7.9 inch bars cover little counter

buyingCriteria.explanation: Measure the underside of the cabinet before choosing a bar, since a bar that is too short leaves dark gaps and one that is too long will not fit. Plan for roughly one bar per cabinet door or per 10 inches of counter you actually use. The Rihvy bars are 8 inches, the YLXS bars are 7.9 inches and the Gritin bar is 10.2 inches. The EZVALO and ZioeYiue both use 10 inch bars. Leave a small margin at each end, since a bar that sits right at the cabinet edge can be knocked loose by a door. Also check for a face frame or lip under the cabinet, which can hide part of a bar from the counter.

A built-in battery is only a convenience if you are not constantly pulling bars down to charge them. Compare milliamp-hours across packs and check the charging port. The EZVALO carries 2400mAh per light, the ZioeYiue has 1800mAh and the YLXS has 1100mAh with USB-C charging. Remember that many small batteries add up to a lot of chargers over a year. A multi-port USB charger on a nearby counter turns the chore into a five minute swap. Label the bars by cabinet so you return each one to its spot.

Warm light near 3000K flatters food and wood, while cool light near 6000K is better for reading labels and cutting. Having three choices lets you match the light to the task. The Gritin spans warm 3000K to cool 6000K, the ZioeYiue offers white, warm and natural, and the Rihvy offers three temperatures through one button. A single fixed tone is simpler but less adaptable. Mixing temperatures across bars in one kitchen looks patchy, so set every bar to the same tone. Check the tone in the evening, since daylight hides differences that appear at night.

The best bars let you pick motion, always-on or off, so a sensor timeout never interrupts real work. Look at how quickly the light turns off after you stop moving. The EZVALO switches off after about 20 seconds, and the MCGOR has a dedicated always-on mode. The Gritin adds a Night Sensing Mode among its four modes. A mode that only wakes in the dark saves charge in a bright kitchen. If you cook under the cabinet most evenings, prefer a steady mode over a short timer.

Metal bodies resist bending and dissipate heat, while plastic bodies save weight. Magnetic mounts need a metal plate on the cabinet, which most packs include. The Gritin uses aluminum alloy and ABS, and the EZVALO mounts magnetically. Dry fit each bar before pressing the adhesive plate in place. Greasy kitchen surfaces defeat adhesive, so degrease the spot with a household cleaner first. Let the plate cure for a day before charging ahead with heavy use.

Under a cabinet, the sensor must catch your hand and body from the front. A 120 degree angle and a 10 ft reach are the common benchmarks. The ZioeYiue detects within 10 ft at 120 degrees, and the EZVALO reaches up to 12 ft. Rihvy pairs motion with a light sensor in AUTO mode so it does not trigger in bright rooms. A passive infrared sensor responds to heat movement, so a stove or oven vent nearby can cause stray triggers. Point the sensor window toward the open counter, not the cooktop.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated capacity and charging convenience. The EZVALO leads at 2400mAh per light, the ZioeYiue follows at 1800mAh with a power display, and the YLXS trails at 1100mAh. Non-detachable batteries were noted as a durability concern.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at LED count, glare control and color range. The Gritin offers 84 LEDs with warm to cool tones, while the MCGOR uses a frosted cover to cut glare. Models with more color and dimming choices scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensor behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared range, angle and timeout. The EZVALO reaches 12 ft and responds in 0.1 seconds, and the ZioeYiue and others use a 10 ft range. We rewarded always-on options that prevent timeouts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and mounting
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked materials and mounting style. The Gritin's metal and ABS body stands out, and magnetic mounts earned credit for tool free installs. Bars that need adhesive only were treated as less flexible.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pack value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what each pack gives you in lights, features and control. The YLXS and EZVALO five packs cover the most ground, while the MCGOR pair is the most basic. Our scores reflect product specs and buyer feedback.

faq.q: How many under-cabinet lights do I need?
faq.a: Plan about one 10 inch bar for each cabinet door or each 10 inches of counter you actually use. A small kitchen often works with three bars, and a full kitchen with five. The EZVALO and YLXS come in five packs, and the ZioeYiue and Rihvy in threes. Buying a pack slightly larger than you need leaves room for a pantry. Overlapping the light from two neighboring bars removes the dark seams that show up on a granite or white counter. Start with the work zones near the sink and cooktop, then add the rest.

faq.q: Do wireless under-cabinet lights drain batteries quickly?
faq.a: It depends on how often the sensor fires and how bright you set them. A light on motion mode used a few times a day lasts far longer than one left on steadily. The ZioeYiue states 8 to 10 hours of use, and the EZVALO has a 2400mAh battery. Dimming a step or two stretches the charge. Always-on use is the biggest drain, so reserve it for cooking sessions. A quick weekly glance at the lights keeps surprises away, and bars with a charge display make that glance easy.

For lightweight bars they are, provided the plate sits flat. Most packs include adhesive metal plates for cabinets that are not magnetic. Press the plate firmly and let it sit before attaching the bar. Wipe the cabinet underside clean first, and avoid spots near the stove where grease collects. A magnet that slides can usually be fixed by moving the plate to a flatter patch of wood.

faq.q: Why does my light turn off while I am still working?
faq.a: Motion mode shuts the bar off after a short timeout, such as the EZVALO's roughly 20 seconds. Switch to always-on mode for long tasks, which the MCGOR, Gritin and EZVALO offer. A small wave of the hand also restarts the timer. Position the sensor so it sees you at the counter, not the wall behind it.

faq.q: Can I replace a worn-out battery?
faq.a: On most of these the battery is built in and cannot be detached. The ZioeYiue states its 1800mAh battery is non-detachable. That means a worn cell means replacing the bar. Avoid leaving the bars fully drained for months, which helps the cell last. If a bar stops holding charge, check the contacts and the cable before giving up on it. Keep a spare pack in mind when buying multipacks, since a single failed bar leaves a visible gap.

faq.q: What color temperature is best for a kitchen?
faq.a: Neutral light between warm and cool suits most kitchens because it shows food colors accurately without feeling harsh. Warm 3000K is cozy but can look yellow on white counters. Cool 6000K is crisp for reading labels. Pick a model with three options, like the Gritin or the Rihvy, and try each for a few evenings before settling on one.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with these lights?
faq.a: Mounting the bar at the back of the cabinet, which throws light onto the wall instead of the counter. Place it toward the front edge and aim it down. Another mistake is forgetting to charge a new set before first use, which the Rihvy listing specifically advises. A full first charge supports better battery health. People also forget to test the sensor angle after mounting, so wave a hand at the counter before you call the job done.
